trigger: GET /api/audit?limit=-1 or MCP query_audit_log {limit:-1} from any AuditLog:Read holder
summary: Negative limit reaches PG as LIMIT -1, errors, and is reported as a store DEGRADE: 503 plus the read-degrade counter YuzuAuditReadDegraded pages on. Any read-privileged client can fire the evidence-availability alert at will.

trigger: backlog probe fails after a cap-bound pass
summary: Doc said the post-delete backlog probe fires after a SUCCESSFUL delete; on PG the whole pass is one txn so the probe failure rolls the DELETE back.

summary: Degraded total reported as the page size — count==total reads as 'this page is the whole trail'. Also raised by cpp-expert (HIGH) and by architect in an earlier round; max severity taken.

trigger: >1h clock divergence between replicas
summary: Cross-replica clock divergence makes two replicas alternate fact sets that never match, each declining. Safe direction, but undocumented.

summary: 25k deletes x 1 pass/hour = 6.94 rows/s drain against a measured 3,801 tps write path; above that the evidence table grows permanently. A full pass measured 41-49ms, so the hour was doing all the damage.

summary: The survivor EXISTS probe flips to a Seq Scan proportional to the backlog (75,823 buffers / 151.8ms at 54% expired on 5M rows). Within the pass timeout; my comment claiming both halves are index-only was wrong and is corrected. The LIMIT-1 subquery rewrite is not applied.

summary: total_count() is an unfiltered aggregate on every request: 13,682 buffers / 191.6ms at 5M rows, ~1.5s at 40M.

summary: action LIKE 'prefix%' is unsargable under en_US.utf8: Parallel Seq Scan, 166,444 buffers / 153.4ms at 5M rows. Wants a text_pattern_ops index.

trigger: deep OFFSET pagination
summary: OFFSET 4,000,000 = 151,113 buffers / 790.7ms; a full paged export is O(n^2/page).

summary: All newly-[pg] cases land in Windows shard B; agent projected 91% of the 600s budget by case count. MEASURED by time instead: this change contributes ~3% of shard B's runtime (B 116.0s -> 113.4s when moved). Rebalanced anyway. Adjudicated MEDIUM, not the platform-leg floor: nothing is observably broken, it is an unverified projection.

trigger: macOS CI leg
summary: macOS leaves YUZU_TEST_POSTGRES_DSN unset so all [pg] cases skip: test_audit_store.cpp went from 0 [pg] cases (fully run on macOS) to 38 (all skipped). macOS coverage of this PR's core surface is now zero.

summary: A test calls YUZU_REQUIRE_PG_DB without a [pg] tag, so it skips in the ~[pg] shard — a partition violation. Untouched by this diff.

trigger: three Gate 3 agents given write access to one worktree
summary: Concurrent agents mutating one shared worktree contaminated each other: cpp-safety built from quality-engineer's in-flight mutation, and a phantom TEST_CASE from a stale object file appeared in a full-suite run. QE discarded and redid all four mutations under a clean-tree discipline. Future runs must give mutating agents their own worktree.

trigger: a fileless replica boots first in a multi-replica deployment and stamps backfill_complete sourcelessly, then a replica holding the real legacy audit.db boots and blindly trusts the marker
summary: Marker authority had no holder-side check: any host trusted backfill_complete once set by ANY process, so a fileless replica winning the boot race permanently foreclosed migration of a sibling's real legacy trail with no recovery path (Sol's diagnosis, corroborated by architect F1 and enterprise-readiness). Fixed by 1a: a host with marker-present + its own legacy file still on disk now re-verifies via fingerprint comparison rather than trusting the marker blindly.

trigger: marker present, this host's own legacy audit.db still on disk, pre-1a code
summary: Pre-1a: a host holding a legacy trail that skipped migration (marker already set by another process) logged at spdlog::debug with no backfill_metric() call -- invisible on the host where the loss occurred and masked fleet-wide in the alert. Verified fixed as a side effect of 1a's redesign: the marker-present+file-present case is now always loud (WARN at entry, then either an ERROR+backfill_metric("failed") refusal on mismatch or an INFO success on a verified retry) -- checked directly against the current code (audit_store.cpp:672-769), no silent debug-only path remains for a host that still holds its trail.

trigger: a foreign/native row occupies an id this legacy file's own resume range also claims
summary: Completion check was a bare COUNT(*), and inserted += batch.size() was unconditional after ON CONFLICT (id) DO NOTHING -- a discarded colliding row was reported as inserted and nothing observed it (architect F2, sharpened by Sol: a bare count is defeated by a foreign writer occupying a claimed id with the total unchanged). Fixed by 1b: PQcmdTuples-based batch_inserted counting plus a whole-file 5-aggregate (count/id-sum/ts-sum/ts-min/ts-max) EQUALITY reconciliation before stamp_complete runs.

trigger: a legacy audit.db that is 0 bytes of junk or otherwise fails to parse as a valid SQLite header
summary: legacy_has_table returning bool folded a prepare/parse ERROR into the same case as a genuinely absent table, so a corrupt legacy file was diagnosed as "fresh install" and its evidence silently forfeited (measured on a 38-byte junk file). Fixed by 1c: typed Present/Absent/Error tri-state; Error now refuses rather than treating corruption as absence.

trigger: two or more replicas' process clocks disagree while sharing one PostgreSQL retention state
summary: Retention decisions compared one replica's own process now against the durable last_pass_now; replicas with disagreeing clocks could alternate BadState/Step fact sets that never matched and each declined forever (sec-F4; Sol's class-level fix). Fixed by 1d: the decision now reads PostgreSQL's own clock inside the same advisory-lock transaction that serialises every sweeper.

trigger: PostgreSQL holds rows with no backfill_complete marker (partial/interrupted backfill) and the legacy file is gone or unusable
summary: A lost marker with no usable source locked out both ordinary boot and break-glass one-shots with no documented recovery (Sol's correction: "permanent" means no product-path recovery, not irrecoverable -- an operator SQL procedure is legitimate). Addressed by the abandon-procedure runbook (fe33b219, further hardened this session in 67110894 to also cover the legacy-file-still-present interaction).

trigger: MCP query_audit_log called with limit <= 0 or a very large limit
summary: Own fix-round defect: the "minimum":1 added to the tool's input schema is decoration -- compiled_input_schemas().at().validate() has one call site, gated on requires_approval(), and AuditLog:Read never requires approval, so an out-of-range limit reached AuditStore::query unclamped and came back as a silent empty page. Fixed via ce8962ba: std::clamp<std::int64_t>(limit, 1, 500), same idiom as query_responses.

trigger: a legacy audit_retention_meta value column holding non-INTEGER text with an embedded NUL
summary: Own fix-round defect: the meta-copy branch read a non-INTEGER value via sqlite3_column_text + an implicit strlen'd std::string(const char*) constructor, silently truncating at the first embedded NUL -- the same trap the row-copy col() lambda 40 lines above already guarded against. Fixed via 243a6d02: sqlite3_column_bytes + explicit-length string construction.

trigger: a retention pass hits the per-pass delete cap and the 5s backlog re-arm fires repeatedly
summary: Own fix-round defect: YuzuAuditRetentionCapBinding's threshold assumed every capped pass is spaced by the full 60-minute cleanup_interval_min, but the 5s backlog re-arm means a genuinely stuck backlog produces thousands of increments within the same window -- the count-based rule fired within ~30 seconds of the first cap hit, not after real sustained overload (measured by performance and confirmed wrong). Fixed via 79733544: a threshold-free "cap-hit recurred every 10-minute slice for a full 30-minute for:" rule.

trigger: the drain-rate ceiling figure quoted in five shipped docs
summary: The quiet-operation drain-rate ceiling was understated by roughly 700x across five shipped docs (audit-log.md, upgrading.md, enterprise-readiness-soc2-first-customer.md, yuzu-alerts.yml, audit-store-clock-guard.md), each reading the figure rather than pattern-matching it forward; the clock-guard runbook went as far as instructing an operator to open an engineering ticket computed from the stale number. Fixed via 8dd12ddb: one canonical home in audit-log.md Capacity, every other site made a pointer.

trigger: a capped retention pass with a real backlog present
summary: The re-arm justification's own cited numbers were wrong -- a capped pass with a real backlog measured 169ms mean / 465ms max, not the 41-49ms cited (that figure was measured with no backlog present, the one state the re-arm never runs in); measured 9.3MB WAL/pass at the 5s cadence, uncited. The deferred LIMIT-1 rewrite (PERF-3) takes the pass to 59.5ms and removes 57-465ms of synchronize_seqscans non-determinism, making the justification true. Fixed via 0dd16d3b (1f).

commit_range: a1dc268c..9531d4c3 (round 3 re-review of the 1a-1f fix diff)
trigger: a REAL (non-sourceless) backfill's stamp_complete call loses the ON CONFLICT (key) DO NOTHING race on backfill_source_fingerprint to another writer (a fileless replica's sourceless stamp, most likely)
summary: stamp_complete's fingerprint INSERT checked only PGRES_COMMAND_OK, not PQcmdTuples -- the same silent-discard class the batch-insert loop already guards against. A real backfill losing the race would report success while a different writer's value sat at the trust anchor, exactly the false-assurance shape the holder-verification redesign exists to prevent. Reported by unhappy-path as SHOULD; independently re-derived HIGH/BLOCKING here (I1 trust-anchor false-assurance + I3 wrong-result-as-success, E0 fires on an ordinary boot-order race, no actor required) per the standing rule that the derived band governs the gate over an agent's native label. Fixed by 70ecfd3f with a dedicated red-green test.
